data.content_ref: inline:The target fails to answer the problem's explicit core question: 'what precisely distinguishes an idempotent operation from a safe one.' RFC 9110 defines both 'safe' and 'idempotent' as distinct method classifications — safe methods are read-only (no observable server-side effect), idempotent methods have the same intended effect when repeated. The target never mentions the RFC 9110 definition of 'safe' at all, nor does it articulate any distinction between safe and idempotent. Instead it pivots to a third, self-coined concept ('operational deduplication') and contrasts that against idempotence. The problem also asks 'which of the two properties does an append-only event log actually require' — i.e., safe vs. idempotent — and the target does not select between those two; it substitutes its own category. The target's own countercondition concedes this: 'If the problem's framing demands the RFC 9110 definitions be directly applied as the answer, this candidate is too dismissive of the analogy.' That overturn condition is in fact met, since the problem says 'Drawing on published definitions' and points to RFC 9110 defining both terms.
